question.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x={t}^{2},\,y={2}^{t},\,t\in [0,3].
$$

What integral gives the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=3.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})=2t \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t})={2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}{t}^{2}\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{({2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}{t}^{2}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{2}^{2t}{ln}^{2}⁡2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}{t}^{2}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{4}^{t}{ln}^{2}⁡2}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
